raw_record.question_text:
$NO_2$ gas is placed in a sealed, evacuated container and allowed to decompose via the following equation:

$2NO_2(g) \leftrightarrow 2NO(g) + O_2(g)$

The graph below indicates the change in concentration for each species over time. How is the rate of the forward reaction changing at t = 60 s?

method.method_draft: First describe the graph: three concentration curves approach horizontal plateaus, and at 60 s the reactant curve is essentially flat. From the text, NO2 is the only gas initially placed in the container, so the curve that starts high and decreases is NO2. Since the forward reaction consumes NO2, relate the forward rate to the NO2 concentration. At 60 s the NO2 concentration is constant on the graph, so the forward rate is not increasing or decreasing; it is remaining constant.
